subject: Logs archive & span-visuals: pricing structure and overage scenarios
messages:
From: Anna K. Reyes <anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@blueriverhealth.com, ethan.morris@blueriverhealth.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning — quick follow-up with two tight asks from our finance and infra teams:

1) We want a blended pricing option for logs archive (cold storage) where the base is a flat monthly credit and overages are capped as a percentage of committed spend. Can you sketch how Redwood would model that vs the regular per-GB metered approach?

2) For tracing/span storage and the advanced dashboards: we need clarity on whether dashboards are licensed per-seat, per-project, or as an add-on slab. We have 8 product users and ~30 consumers who will view dashboards — prefer not to license all viewers.

Please send a short matrix and an example invoice scenario for our procurement review. Also, include any pilot terms (30–60 day) you can extend.

Appreciate it,
Anna
Director of Platform Engineering
Blue River Health

--
Attachment: requirements_summary_BluRiver.pdf (pdf stub)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Anna K. Reyes <anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Hi Anna — thanks, this is clear. High-level reply and I'll attach a draft matrix:

- Cold archive: we can offer a hybrid slab model. Option A: monthly credit (committed GB pool) + overage billed at a reduced per-GB rate with a soft cap of 25% over committed spend for the first 12 months; Option B: pure metered. I'll include modeled invoices for both.

- Traces & dashboards: two paths we typically propose: (1) seat-based for contributors + viewer license bundle (cheap viewer token) or (2) project-based dashboard bundles priced by active trace retention tier (better if you have many viewers). Given your 8 product users / 30 viewers, Option 2 may save you if views are mostly consumers.

I'll run numbers with Ben for a 12-month commitment and return the xlsx, plus a 30-day pilot SOW for the dashboard pilot.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood-pricing-matrix-BRH-draft.xlsx (xlsx stub)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Anna K. Reyes <anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Anna — I pulled together a modeled invoice for a 12-month commit at two commitment sizes and included the overage math (attached). Highlights:

- Commit A (modest): 5 TB/month credit, overage at $0.015/GB, soft cap 25% — estimated monthly invoice (inc. dashboards pilot) $6.9k.
- Commit B (aggressive): 20 TB/month credit, overage at $0.009/GB, cap 15% — estimated monthly invoice $18.2k.

Dashboards licensing: we recommend project-bundles for your profile. Project-bundles come with 10 contributor seats and unlimited low-cost viewer tokens; additional contributor seats are $75/mo.

Also attaching a 30-day pilot SOW that scopes up to 2 dashboards and 14 days of retention backfill for traces. We can push pilot start within two weeks pending PO.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW-visibility-pilot-BRH-v1.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@blueriverhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@blueriverhealth.com, anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Thanks Marissa / Ben — a few follow-ups from procurement:

- Can Redwood commit to a true dollar cap on monthly overage rather than a percent for Commit A? Finance prefers a hard cap (e.g., $2,000/mo) for budget certainty.
- How would change-of-terms work if we scale to Commit B mid-contract? Any true-up windows?
- For dashboards, can we license only the 8 contributors and enable SSO-based viewer tokens billed at a nominal rate only for active viewers? We'd prefer not to buy unlimited viewer rights.

If you can update the matrix with the hard cap option and a change-of-commit clause, procurement can route a PO fast.

Ethan
Director, Procurement
Blue River Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@blueriverhealth.com>, anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 13:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Ethan — we can do both the hard-dollar cap and a predictable mid-contract scale path. Proposed contract language (summary):

- Hard cap: For Commit A we can set a monthly overage cap of $2,000 for months 1–12. Any usage beyond the cap will be handled via a short-term credit arrangement and reviewed at quarterly business reviews.
- True-up / scale: We include two scale checkpoints (month 3 and month 9) where usage will be reviewed; if you exceed threshold X at checkpoint we will offer a one-time true-up to move you to Commit B pricing pro-rated for the remainder of the term.
- Viewer licensing: we can enable SSO-based viewer tokens that are billed only when the token is active in a billing period. We'll model that as a $3/active-viewer/month on top of the contributor seats.

I'll loop Kimberly for legal/pricing verbiage for the SOW. If this looks acceptable I can generate a redline-ready term sheet and provisional PO template.

Best,
Marissa

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@blueriverhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, procurement@blueriverhealth.com, anna.reyes@blueriverhealth.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Logs/archive and traces: pricing shape questions

Ethan — adding legal language inline so procurement can drop into your template: 

1) Overage Cap: "For the first 12 months of the Agreement, Customer's total billed overage related to Logs Archive shall not exceed $2,000 per month. Should usage exceed the hard cap, Redwood and Customer will engage in a commercially reasonable review to agree on additional capacity or credits."

2) Mid-term True-up: "The Agreement will include two review windows (Day 90, Day 270). If aggregate monthly usage exceeds 140% of committed capacity at a review window, Redwood will offer a pro-rated upgrade to the next commit level with credit for the unused portion of prior commitments."

3) Viewer tokens: "Viewer tokens issued via SSO will be metered and billed only for tokens that are active in a monthly billing period at a rate of $3 per active viewer per month. Contributor seats are charged per active user per month at the agreed contributor rate."

I'll export a redline-friendly term sheet and tuck these clauses into the SOW. If procurement sends a PO with the provisional commit line item and desired pilot start date, legal can prioritize a quick signature.

Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing & Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
